title: Recordanelles for transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording in human cells - Nature Biotechnology
gist: The recordanelle is a single-protein synthetic organelle (mitochondrial anchor, condensate assembler, poly(A)-binding protein) that stores up to 90% of expressed mRNAs in human cells and protects them for days. In HEK293T cells, recordanelleV2 preserved doxycycline-induced and interferon-beta transcriptional responses 2 to 5 days after the stimulus ended, including at single-cell resolution, without detectable change to the transcriptome, proteome or mitochondrial function.

insights.claim: Existing transcriptomics either gives a destructive snapshot or a low-resolution history for a few genes, and DNA-based recorders have been largely confined to prokaryotes or small gene sets, leaving no nondisruptive, unbiased, transcriptome-wide recorder for eukaryotic cells.

insights.claim: A recordanelle is one protein combining a generic RNA-binding domain, a biomolecular condensate assembler and a mitochondrial membrane anchor, which collects endogenous cytoplasmic RNAs in a protective condensate attached to mitochondria so they survive time and cell division.

insights.claim: The authors position recordanelles as complementary to TimeVault, a vault-particle recorder predominantly tested for 24-hour expression snapshots, arguing recordanelles continuously sample the transcriptome over arbitrary time windows and suit questions beyond 24 hours where the timing of interest is unknown.
